question: At a 55-mph curve, when must a no-passing zone be marked, and what happens if the next no-passing zone begins less than 400 feet later?
model_answer: Direct Answer: On a roadway with center line markings, a no-passing zone must be marked at the curve if the passing sight distance is less than the minimum value shown in Table 3B-1 for the 85th-percentile speed or the speed limit (the specific 55-mph value from Table 3B-1 is not included in the evidence provided). The evidence provided contains no provision addressing what happens when the next no-passing zone begins less than 400 feet later, so that part of the question cannot be answered from this evidence. Standards (mandatory): - "On roadways with center line markings, no-passing zone markings shall be used at horizontal or vertical curves where the passing sight distance is less than the minimum shown in Table 3B-1 for the 85th-percentile speed or the speed limit." - "On two-way, two-lane or three-lane roadways where center line markings are installed, no-passing zones shall be established at vertical and horizontal curves and other locations where an engineering study indicates that passing must be prohibited because of inadequate sight distances or other special conditions." - "When used, the NO PASSING ZONE sign shall be installed on the left-hand side of the roadway at the beginning of no-passing zones identified by pavement markings or DO NOT PASS signs or both." Citations: - Section 3B.03 Standard §4 (p.543) - Section 3B.03 Standard §3 (p.543) - Section 2C.53 Standard §1 (p.191)
gold_answer: The no-passing zone must be marked when available passing sight distance is less than 900 feet. If successive no-passing zones are separated by less than 400 feet, the markings should connect them.
